statusHelp.prospective: Prospective: registered but not evaluated yet. Do not rely on this supplier yet.
statusHelp.under_evaluation: Under evaluation: an evaluation is in progress.
statusHelp.approved: Approved: the supplier met your requirements at the last evaluation.
statusHelp.conditional: Conditionally approved: approved with conditions that must be followed up, for at most six months.
statusHelp.suspended: Suspended: do not place new orders until the issues are resolved.
statusHelp.rejected: Rejected: the supplier did not meet your requirements.

form.newSubtitle: Register a supplier. It has the status "Prospective" until an evaluation has approved it.
form.readOnly: You can view this supplier but not change it.
form.countryHint: The country where the supplier is registered.
form.profileHint: Tick what applies. The answers decide which assessments the supplier needs.
form.intervalHint: Leave empty to use the default for {{ level }} criticality ({{ months }} months).
form.nextEvaluationHint: Set automatically when an evaluation is decided. Set it here only to override.
form.changeReasonHint: Saved in the revision history so others can see why the record changed.
form.invalidCountry: Not recognised as countries: {{ values }}. Remove them and pick countries from the list.
form.locationsReview: Check these locations: {{ codes }}. They were saved before countries were picked from a list and may have been shortened from a country name (for example IR is Iran, not Ireland). Saving the form confirms them.
form.transferNeeded: Personal data stored in {{ countries }} leaves the EU/EEA without an adequacy decision. Register a transfer assessment.

criticalityMeaning.low: Low: easy to replace, little harm if it fails. Re-evaluated every {{ months }} months by default.
criticalityMeaning.medium: Medium: a failure is a nuisance but you can work around it. Re-evaluated every {{ months }} months by default.
criticalityMeaning.high: High: a failure hits your products, services or information hard. Re-evaluated every {{ months }} months by default.
criticalityMeaning.critical: Critical: you cannot deliver without it, or it holds your most sensitive data. Re-evaluated every {{ months }} months by default.

form.profileNeeds: Besides the approval, this supplier needs: {{ kinds }}.

detail.notFound: This supplier does not exist or you do not have access to it.
detail.intervalOwn: Every {{ months }} months (set for this supplier)
detail.intervalDefault: Every {{ months }} months (default for {{ criticality }} criticality)
detail.riskFlags: What the supplier does for us
detail.deleteMessage: {{ code }} {{ name }} will be removed with its evaluations and performance log. The audit trail keeps a record.
detail.transferNeededBody: This supplier processes personal data in a country outside the EU/EEA without an adequacy decision. Register the transfer with its legal basis (for example signed standard contractual clauses) and a transfer impact assessment.

statusDialog.title: Change supplier status
statusDialog.hint: Approval normally comes from a decided evaluation. Change the status by hand when something happens between evaluations, for example a suspension after a serious incident.
statusDialog.approvalOnly: Only people with approval rights can move a supplier into or out of approved, conditional, suspended or rejected.
statusDialog.approvalNote: This change counts as an approval decision and is recorded as yours.

evaluations.title: Evaluations
evaluations.none: An evaluation answers a questionnaire and ends in a decision. Start one to approve the supplier.
evaluations.kindSetsStatus: The decision sets the supplier's approval status and schedules the next re-evaluation.
evaluations.kindRecordsOnly: This assessment is recorded for its type and does not change the supplier's status.

evaluationsPage.title: Supplier evaluations
evaluationsPage.subtitle: Every evaluation and assessment: what is waiting for answers or a decision, and what has been decided.
evaluationsPage.noneOpen: Nothing is waiting for answers or a decision. Decided evaluations are under "All".

evaluation.notFound: This evaluation does not exist or you do not have access to it.
evaluation.submitNoSummaryMessage: The evaluation has no summary. The person who decides only sees the score and the answers. Add a summary first, or submit anyway.
evaluation.reopenMessage: The evaluation goes back to draft so the answers can be changed.
evaluation.cancelMessage: A cancelled evaluation is kept for the record, but can no longer be answered or decided.
evaluation.deleteMessage: "{{ title }}" will be removed. The audit trail keeps a record.
evaluation.unanswered: {{ count }} required questions are not answered yet. They are marked below.
evaluation.advisory: The score and recommendation are advice. A person with approval rights makes the decision.
evaluation.questionsHint: Answers are kept for questions that stay. New questions start unanswered.
evaluation.summaryPlaceholder: Sum up the strengths, the weaknesses and what you expect from the supplier.
evaluation.scoreMeaning: The score is the weighted share of points (0–100). At {{ pass }} or more, with no critical question failed, the recommendation is to approve.
evaluation.raiseDeviationHint: A failed critical question or a rejection is a nonconformity. Register it as a deviation so it is followed up.

decide.title: Decide the evaluation
decide.advisory: You decide. The recommendation only reflects the answers.
decide.setsStatus: This decision sets the supplier's status and schedules the next re-evaluation.
decide.recordsOnly: This decision is recorded for the assessment type. The supplier's status does not change.
decide.conditionsHint: What the supplier must do, and by when. The supplier owner gets a follow-up task.
decide.nextEvaluationHint: Leave empty to use the supplier's interval. Conditional approvals are re-evaluated within six months.

questions.weightHint: How much the question counts in the score (1–10).
questions.criticalHint: A "No" (or 0 points) means rejection, whatever the score.
questions.refsHint: When the evaluation is decided, it documents these requirements. Up to {{ max }}.

questionnaires.title: Questionnaires
questionnaires.subtitle: The sets of questions used to evaluate suppliers. Built-in sets cover every type, each question mapped to the requirements it checks. You can add your own.
questionnaires.name: Name
questionnaires.focusPlaceholder: For example data outside the EU
questionnaires.deleteMessage: "{{ name }}" will be removed. Evaluations already started keep their questions.

performance.title: Performance log
performance.none: Nothing logged yet. Log deliveries, quality problems and incidents to build the basis for the next re-evaluation.
performance.deleteMessage: "{{ title }}" will be removed from the performance log.

stats.period: Figures for the last {{ days }} days.

form.title: What happened
form.deviationPlaceholder: Search deviations by code or title
form.deviationHint: Went wrong? After saving, use "Register deviation" on the entry so it is followed up.

warning.title: Results are weak
warning.on_time: Less than {{ threshold }} % of deliveries were on time.
warning.quality: Less than {{ threshold }} % of deliveries had the agreed quality.
warning.deviation: A deviation is linked to the supplier.

prompts.overview: Give me an overview of our supplier register: which suppliers need follow-up, which critical ones are not approved, which process personal data without a DPA, and what should I do first?
prompts.summarise: Summarise this supplier: status, latest evaluations, open conditions, agreements and data processing, recent performance and what needs follow-up.
prompts.nextStep: Based on the supplier's status, evaluations and agreements, what should happen next, and why?
prompts.criticality: How should I decide how critical a supplier is? Explain low, medium, high and critical with examples.
prompts.explainScore: Explain how this evaluation is scored, what the recommendation means and which answers pulled the score down.
prompts.evaluationPriorities: Which supplier evaluations are overdue or waiting for a decision, and which should I take first?
prompts.dataLocations: Which of these data locations are outside the EU/EEA, and what do I need for a lawful transfer?
prompts.certificates: Which certificates should I ask this kind of supplier for, and what should I check on them?
